about: Trade practice the build follows where the documents are silent or wrong (Q6216): how each trade runs or places what the drawings leave out, and what the field installs where a drawn value can't be built. Order of authority: the documents, then the code (coderules.json and each trade's rules data, cited here where a rule uses a code number), then this file. Each rule: its id, the trade, what it fills in or corrects, its numbers, and its basis: the reason every object it lays in or value it corrects carries, so nothing it makes passes for drawn.

rules.fills: a roof whose roof plan outline falls short of the storey under it: the roof is built over the storey's whole floor plate, its slope and parapet the plan's, the plan's outline kept as the design value
rules.basis: trade practice: a roof covers the whole building under it, out to (and onto) its outside walls; a roof plan line well inside the walls is a roof area, cricket or slope line drawn on the roof, not its edge, and the roofer and framer carry the roof to the walls

rules.fills: a roof level's framing where the roof plans name trusses or joists: the members across the roof's short way at their spacing, as deep as the notes say, bearing on the walls at the level's elevation (its top of plate or truss bearing), the deck on them, the outside walls carried up round them to the deck or the parapet (numbers: spacing_in and depth_in when a note gives none; chord_in, a member's width; deck_in, the deck and roofing over the members when no roof sheathing or deck note gives its thickness (deck_words name the deck in a note, deck_not_words mark another deck's note, deck_stop_words start its fastening, deck_min_in..deck_max_in the thicknesses a deck can be); min_span_ft, the shortest piece kept)
rules.basis: trade practice: pre-engineered wood roof trusses (and open-web joists) are set at 24" on centre across the building's short way, bearing on the outside walls' top plate, at least 24" deep for a flat or low-slope roof; the sheathing and roofing go on their top chords, and the outside walls (or a parapet) close the truss space round the edge

rules.fills: where a framed floor's joists bear between its outside walls: each joist line is cut at the bearing lines of the storey's walls under it that run across the joists, and each span is its own piece (numbers: line_fraction, the share of the floor's length a line of walls runs to be a bearing line; line_tol_in, walls this close are one line; angle_tol_deg, a wall this near square to the joists runs across them; min_span_ft, the shortest span kept; end_bearing_ft, a bearing line this near the floor's edge is the joists' end bearing, the joists running on over it to the edge in one piece (a cantilever); words: bearing_words a wall type that carries the floor, non_bearing_words one that doesn't)
rules.basis: trade practice: floor joists span between bearing lines (the outside walls, interior bearing walls, beams and a double-loaded corridor's walls), each span a joist of its own lapped or butted over the bearing; a wall line running most of the building's length across the joists carries them (its doors under headers) whatever stud the partition legend names (the structure's notes govern what bears), a wall typed non-bearing or a partition line the rooms break up does not; a joist runs on over a bearing near the floor's edge to the edge (a cantilever), one piece

rules.fills: what each level's floor element is built of and how thick: a slab its slab notes' (or the design's) thickness; a framed floor its topping and deck, the joists under it their own members (words: slab_marks, a slab's thickness written before one of them, slab_lead, one written after it; separators, the words between a layered note's layers, top to bottom; lead_words, words a layer's thickness may follow (`NOMINAL 3/4"`); name_skip and name_stop, the words a layer's name drops before it and ends at; topping_words, deck_words, member_words, what a layer is; skip_words, a layer naming a spacing or fastening, not a thickness; numbers: the inches a layer of each kind may be; a framed floor's deck its notes don't give is the trade rules' subfloor, framing.subfloor_in)
rules.basis: trade practice: a floor is built as its documents describe it, per level: a slab on grade or a structural slab is its noted thickness; a wood-framed floor is a topping (gypsum concrete or another poured underlayment) on a sheathing deck on joists or floor trusses, the deck the floor's surface under the topping and the joists their own members under it; a 3/4" (23/32") rated sheathing is the usual deck where the notes give none; where nothing gives the floor its build-up the build's default slab is used and marked a default

rules.fills: a sloped roof's deck (or an unframed roof's slab): one thickness normal to its slope, its underside parallel to its top, on the framing's top chords, which follow the slope along and across the members; an unframed sloped roof whose underside rises over the walls under it has the outside walls carried up to it
rules.basis: trade practice: a wood or metal roof deck is a sheet of one thickness laid on the framing, the sloped joists or truss top chords setting the slope; only a flat structure with tapered fill or tapered insulation is a wedge, and that is its own layer; the outside walls close the space under a sloped roof's high side

rules.fills: where a panelboard or switchboard stands when a plan draws it: the rectangle its label sits on or beside (numbers: label_reach_h text heights plus reach_ft feet from the label; a footprint depth_in and length_in in range, its long side at least min_ratio times its depth; panel_height_in and switchboard_height_in when no submittal gives the box)
rules.basis: trade practice: the electrician sets gear where the plans draw it, the drawn rectangle its footprint and the wall it touches the one it hangs or stands on; a schedule's LOCATION only names the room, so it places only gear no plan draws (and that placement is proposed)

rules.fills: a ceiling luminaire's place where the electrical plan's symbol and the reflected ceiling plan's light differ (numbers: reach_ft, the farthest a light is moved; connect_reach_ft, a light this close is at its spot)
rules.basis: trade practice: the electrician sets each ceiling light where the architect's reflected ceiling plan draws and dimensions it, the ceiling's layout aligning lights, sprinklers and sensors; the electrical plan's symbols show which lights and circuits, not where to the inch

rules.fills: a fixture's cold or hot water branch, or a room's branches, no plan joins to a main (numbers: plumbing.json fill_in)
rules.basis: trade practice: each fixture's or room's water branch is teed off the nearest main of its system at right angles, the fixtures of one room and back-to-back rooms on one wet wall sharing one branch; a fixture branch nothing sizes is 1/2 inch (IPC Table 604.5)

rules.fills: a fixture's waste arm no plan joins to a drain line of its floor
rules.basis: trade practice: a fixture's waste arm runs from its trap to the nearest drain line of its floor at right angles and falls to it at the code's slope (IPC 704.1); it is the fixture's trap size (IPC Table 709.1: water closet 3 in., shower and urinal 2 in., clothes washer 2 in., tub, sink and laundry tray 1-1/2 in., lavatory 1-1/4 in.)

rules.fills: a fixture's vent no plan joins to a vent line or stack of its floor
rules.basis: trade practice: each fixture's trap is vented by a vent taken up its wet wall and over to the nearest vent line of its floor (IPC 901.2, 906.1 trap-to-vent distance); a vent is at least half its drain's size and not under 1-1/4 in. (IPC 916.2)

rules.fills: a branch circuit's raceway or cable path: the drawings show its devices and a homerun arrow, not the path
rules.basis: trade practice: a circuit's devices are joined device to device in a square tree above the ceiling, the homerun takes the corridor to its panel's top entry (rules: conduitroute.json; fill and box fill per NEC Ch. 9 and 314.16)

rules.fills: a notification appliance circuit's cable: the drawings show the appliances (and the shop drawings their circuit and address), not the wiring between them
rules.basis: trade practice: each NAC is one power-limited cable chained appliance to appliance from its power supply or the control panel, in address order where the shop drawings give it, else nearest neighbour; a circuit is closed where its load passes the output's rating at 80% or its voltage drop leaves the last appliance under 16 V (Class B, the end-of-line device at the last appliance; NFPA 72 12.3, 18.3; NEC 760.154; rules: fawiring.json)

rules.fills: a signaling line circuit's cable (and the annunciator's bus): the drawings show the initiating devices and modules, not the loop through them
rules.basis: trade practice: the control panel's addressable loop runs device to device storey by storey up the riser over the panel, in address order where the shop drawings give it, else nearest neighbour, a new loop past the loop's device capacity; Class B with T-taps allowed unless the documents call for Class A (NFPA 72 12.3, 23.6; NEC 760.154; rules: fawiring.json)

rules.fills: a NAC power supply where a storey's notification load needs one and no document places it, and its start circuit from the control panel
rules.basis: trade practice: a NAC power supply (booster) serves its storey's appliances where the control panel's own outputs can't carry them, as many as the load needs at 4 outputs each, in a service room nearest the riser, started by the control panel and on its own dedicated 120 V branch circuit (NFPA 72 10.6.5); the shop drawings place them (rules: fawiring.json)

rules.fills: the fire alarm control panel where the model has fire alarm devices and no document places the panel
rules.basis: trade practice: every fire alarm system has a control panel (NFPA 72 10.4), set in the fire command, electrical or mechanical room of the lowest storey it serves, its top at 72 in (rules: fawiring.json)

rules.fills: a circuit's route estimated from its homerun tag where the model could not route it
rules.basis: trade practice: a homerun the drawings mark by an arrow only is run along the plan's axes to its panel, a placeholder until it is routed

rules.fills: a power device no document puts on a circuit
rules.basis: trade practice: a device the documents leave off every circuit goes on a spare circuit of the nearest panel of its level, its homerun along the plan's axes in the ceiling space to the panel (NEC 210.11: every outlet is on a branch circuit)

rules.fills: an air terminal no duct of its system reaches
rules.basis: trade practice: each diffuser, register or grille is taken off the nearest duct of its system by a round branch at right angles at the duct's height, then down to the terminal at its neck size

rules.fills: a duct through a rated wall where the documents tag no damper
rules.basis: code: a duct penetrating a fire-resistance-rated assembly takes a fire damper (IMC 607.5); the field installs one at the wall in the duct's size; alternative: an exception of IMC 607.5 (a fire partition in a sprinklered building, a listed through-penetration) that the engineer may confirm instead

rules.fills: the unit serving an air terminal no duct of the model leads to a unit from and no schedule row names the room of
rules.basis: trade practice: a room's own air unit (a PTAC, a fan coil, a split system's indoor unit; a bath exhaust fan for its exhaust grille) serves the room's terminals of its air; alternative: a central unit the engineer's duct layout ties it to

rules.fills: a return grille no return duct of its floor reaches
rules.basis: trade practice: a return grille the drawings leave unducted returns through the ceiling plenum to its unit (IMC 602 plenum); alternative: a ducted return the engineer may call for

rules.fills: each room's ceiling height, from the first source in `order` that gives one (numbers: clear_ft, the least ceiling height a derived one is set to; default_size_in, the depth of the floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly over a room when its framing is not read; deck_in, the deck or topping over the members; membrane_in, the ceiling's channel and board under them)
rules.basis: trade practice: the reflected ceiling plans set ceiling heights; a room takes its own RCP tag or note first, then the enlarged plan or unit RCP of its room type, then its ceiling type's legend, then a section or interior elevation that dimensions it; only where none gives one is it derived, at the underside of the assembly over the room (the floor to floor less the members, deck and ceiling membrane), never under the least ceiling height the code allows (IBC 1208.2: 7'-6" in habitable spaces and corridors); a derived height is inferred, marked as such with its basis, and asked of the architect; alternative: the height the architect gives

rules.fills: a mezzanine's elevation where the sections and elevations mark none, and the floor to floor of the storey it is in where none is read (numbers: clear_ft, the clear height kept under and over a mezzanine; default_size_in, the depth of its floor's structure)
rules.basis: trade practice: a mezzanine is a partial floor set about halfway up the storey it is in, the storey running past it to the floor or roof above; the code keeps at least 7 ft clear under and over it (IBC 505.2), so a storey under a mezzanine is at least twice that plus the mezzanine's structure; alternative: the elevation the sections or the architect give

rules.fills: a column the grid crossing implies where the plans draw none
rules.basis: trade practice: a structural grid crossing carries a column where the structural plans show the grid but no column outline

rules.fills: a raceway that meets another trade's duct or pipe, or another raceway, at its height where no tier of the ceiling space clears it
rules.basis: trade practice: the electrician offsets the raceway under the obstacle (over it where under would drop into the ceiling) with the clearance the routing keeps, a field offset at each side (rules: conduitroute.json clearances)

rules.fills: a panel whose allowed entry window can't take the raceways routed to it
rules.basis: trade practice: where a panel's top (or bottom) can't take its raceways, the electrician sets a pull box or wireway on it that they land in; an angle pull box is at least six times the largest raceway plus the others in the row (NEC 314.28(A)(2)); alternative: an extension gutter or a larger can

rules.fills: a product field the documents disagree on (the submittal against the schedule or the specification)
rules.basis: trade practice: the field installs what the approved submittal names; where it differs from the drawings' schedule or the specification, the schedule's value is kept beside it as the design value and the difference stays listed for the engineer

rules.fills: a device or junction box too small for what enters it (box fill)
rules.basis: code: a box's volume holds its conductors, devices, clamps and grounds by NEC 314.16(B); the field installs the next larger box of NEC Table 314.16(A), or adds an extension ring

rules.fills: two holes bored closer in one framing member than the hole rule allows
rules.basis: trade practice: holes in a member keep the maker's spacing (the hole rule's multiple of the larger hole); where two raceways would cross a member closer than that, the field bores one hole sized for both where the hole rule takes it at that distance from the bearing (NEC 300.4(A)(1) protection kept), else bores them a bay apart

rules.fills: a raceway too small for its conductors (fill over NEC Chapter 9 Table 1)
rules.basis: code: conductors fill at most 40 percent of a raceway of three or more (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1); the field pulls them in the next trade size that holds them (NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5)

rules.fills: branch conductors too small for their length (voltage drop over 3 percent)
rules.basis: code and practice: branch circuit conductors are sized for at most 3 percent voltage drop (NEC 210.19(A) Informational Note 4), the drawings' length table first; the field pulls the next conductor size

rules.fills: the roof curb a ducted rooftop unit (an outdoor air unit, a packaged rooftop unit, an air handler, an energy recovery unit, a roof exhaust fan) stands on where the schedule and plans give none (numbers: default_size_in, the curb's height above the roof; sizes: by the unit's kind or schedule words)
rules.basis: trade practice: a ducted rooftop unit is set on its manufacturer's roof curb (its supply and return or its plenum through the curb), flashed to the roof with the curb's top at least 8 in over the finished roof; the stock curb is 14 in high

rules.fills: the stand or rails a rooftop unit with no duct through the roof (a heat pump's or condensing unit's outdoor section, a split system's) sits on where the schedule and plans give none (sizes: the kinds set on a stand and its height; a kind no row names goes on a curb, M-ROOF-CURB)
rules.basis: trade practice: an outdoor heat pump or condensing unit on a roof is set on an equipment stand or rails off the roof membrane, high enough for the roof to be worked under it and clear of snow and ponding; 18 in is the usual stand

rules.fills: the refrigerant line set between a split system's outdoor unit and the indoor unit its schedule row pairs it with, where no plan draws its route (numbers: default_size_in, the suction line's size)
rules.basis: trade practice: the outdoor unit's suction and liquid lines run to the indoor unit its schedule pairs it with, laid over the roof to above that unit, then down to it; where the plans' notes give a route (a chase, a sleeve) that route governs and this one is for review

rules.fills: where a piece of mechanical equipment sits and how tall it is when its schedule, submittal and plans give no height (mountings: by the equipment's kind and its schedule's words, the first row that fits; at above_ceiling = its bottom gap_in over the room's ceiling, the body in the plenum; at floor = its bottom bottom_in over the floor, kept under the ceiling; height_in when the schedule prints none; a kind no row names stands on the floor at the usual size of its kind; a roof unit is on its curb or stand, M-ROOF-CURB / M-ROOF-STAND; a schedule's mounting height or AFF governs over every row)
rules.basis: trade practice: mechanical equipment is set where its kind is made to go, not stood on the floor: a ceiling exhaust fan's housing is above the ceiling with its grille in it, a damper is in its duct above the ceiling, a packaged terminal unit is through the exterior wall in its sleeve on its electrical sub-base, a unit heater hangs high clear of heads; alternative: a mounting the schedule, a submittal or a plan note gives

mountings.basis: a roof fan stands on its roof or curb
a wall exhaust fan is high in its wall, its top at the ceiling at most
a ceiling exhaust fan's housing is above the ceiling, its grille in it
an exhaust fan inside the building is the ceiling cabinet kind: its housing above the ceiling, its grille in it
a damper is in its duct above the ceiling, reached through an access panel
a terminal unit hangs in its duct above the ceiling
a horizontal unit hangs above the ceiling
a packaged terminal unit is through the exterior wall in its sleeve, set on its electrical sub-base (makers' sub-bases are about 3-1/2 to 4 in), about 16 in high
a cabinet unit heater stands at the floor or is recessed low in the wall
a unit heater hangs high, its bottom about 7 ft over the floor clear of heads and its top at the ceiling at most

rules.fills: the exhaust risers a typical riser detail draws: each fan's duct from where its room's view ends it in the chase, up the chase to just under the roof deck, across to the roof terminal the roof plan places over that chase and up into it (numbers: reach_ft, how far in plan the terminal may be from the chase it serves once the roof plan is lined up with the chases; clear_ft, how far under the roof deck the ducts turn to the terminal; default_size_in, a fan duct's size where none is read; duct_gap_in, the gap between side-by-side ducts in one chase)
rules.basis: trade practice: a typical riser detail is built at every chase its roof terminal stands over (the plans key one instance); where the notes require each exhaust duct to be continuous to the outside, every fan keeps its own duct to the terminal (side by side in the chase), else the chase carries one riser of the fans' combined duct area

rules.fills: where a wall-mounted device goes when its height would put any part of it above its room's finished ceiling (numbers: min_below_in, the least clearance from its top to the ceiling; below, a kind's own clearance by its kinds or words; legend_words, the words after a legend's or schedule's height that make it the device's clearance under the ceiling; skip_kinds, kinds whose place above a ceiling is their own; skip_from, the height sources that put a device somewhere other than on a wall)
rules.basis: trade practice: a wall-mounted device is installed on the wall below the finished ceiling of the room it serves, where it can be seen, reached and serviced, never in the plenum over it; its top is at least its own clearance under the ceiling (an exit sign or emergency light the legend's or schedule's "x in below ceiling", else 2 in); a device whose height (a default, a rule, or a document that does not fit the room) puts any part above the ceiling is set at the highest allowed place and reported, its design height kept beside; alternative: a ceiling-mounted version of the device, which the engineer may call for instead

rules.fills: where an equipment connection goes when its plan's mark names a piece of equipment built on another level or elsewhere (a roof unit's circuit tagged on a plan under it)
rules.basis: trade practice: an equipment connection is made at its equipment (its disconnect or junction box on the unit, at the unit's side half way up); a mark naming the unit follows the unit, never the room under it

rules.fills: where the connection of a piece of ceiling equipment is built (a ceiling exhaust fan's, an above-ceiling unit's), every time the model is built: at the housing of the equipment it serves, as the equipment and the ceiling over it stand then, never at a height fixed earlier (numbers: reach_ft, how far from where its plan puts the connection its equipment may be; tolerance_in, how far from its housing a connection may be and still be at it; clear_in, how far above the ceiling's underside the box's bottom is at least, over the ceiling board)
rules.basis: trade practice: the connection of ceiling equipment is made at the equipment's wiring compartment on its housing, above the ceiling in the plenum (NEC 314.29: the box stays accessible, through the equipment or the ceiling; NEC 300.11: wiring above a ceiling is supported there, not by the ceiling), never hung exposed under the finished ceiling nor standing off the housing it serves
